liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Highlights a cheerful jam roughly 18:10 to 20:40, followed by a darker, scary stretch; some hiss throughout; Enjoyable, with a nice groove throughout; Brokedown Palace is also praised as sweet [7][9][17]
- **Playing in the Band** (1 review): Opens the second set with a jazzy performance featuring Keith all over the keys [17]
- **Going Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): Reviewer calls it the best version ever, with Phil prominent; advises playing loud [13]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-11-26.127478.sbd.restore.droncit.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 26 songs; 174 min; rated 4/5 by 7 [1]. Said about its sound: Restored version greatly improves the fidelity over earlier, poorer-sounding copies of this show; Sounds like a cassette recorded with a dirty head and automatic level control; hissy, dead, with mechanical noise, mostly reduced now [1][16]
- **gd72-11-26.sbd.cotsman.9248.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 172 min; rated 3.92/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer found this soundboard pretty low in quality, with no hidden gem; First fifteen or so tracks are hissy and distorted; from Jack Straw onward levels settle and sound improves, with some hiss; Early portion sounds muffled, like listening with earplugs, though every instrument on stage is audible; reviewer had worse analog tapes [6][9][10][13]
- **gd1972-11-26.152827.sbd-remaster.acetboy.flac1644**: soundboard; 25 songs; 168 min [4]
- **gd1972-11-26.158749.sbd.menke.miller.fix.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 172 min [3]

## Around the show

- The band tuned to 'Beer Barrel Polka' and 'Zippedy Doo Dah' before this song [3]
- Tunings of 'Beer Barrel Polka' and 'Zippedy Doo Dah' came before this song [4]
- Considered another great 1972 Texas show, perhaps the weakest of them, yet still great; Jerry builds steam late in set one [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-11-26.127478.sbd.restore.droncit.flac16**: transferred by Dan McDonald; source: SBD [1]. Also: David Lemieux says the vault holds only a cassette of this show, despite earlier listings citing a master reel [1]
- **gd72-11-26.sbd.cotsman.9248.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: A seven-second splice was inserted at about 20:08 in the Dark Star; Reviewer once had this on tape, obtained from Ron Elner via Tom Norton; Soundboard transferred via MR and DAT to CD, then EAC to SHN, with edits by J. Cotsman [2][7][8]
- **gd1972-11-26.152827.sbd-remaster.acetboy.flac1644**: transferred by acetboy  2021-07-07; source: remaster of shn #9248 with short patches from shn #123022. [4]. Also: Remaster whose notes refer to an earlier remaster stating a cassette source [4]
- **gd1972-11-26.158749.sbd.menke.miller.fix.flac16**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 26, 2022; source: SBD > Master Reel > Reel > PCM > DAT (44.1k) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerrybase: [Grateful Dead – 1972-11-26](https://jerrybase.com/events/19721126-01) [19]
